replication.target_description: Unresolved row correspondence among printed candidate RMET condition effects, ART predictors and/or interactions.

reported_success.quote: we found no support for any short-term ... causal effects of reading literary fiction on theory of mind.

notes: Identity verified from the supplied full primary replication article: matching title, all seven authors and DOI 10.1037/pspa0000064 on page 1; nine text pages include Methods, Results, Discussion and References. Header has provisional volume/issue/pagination (Vol. 111, No. 9, 000), unlike the final bibliographic issue, but title/authors/DOI identify the work. No PDF was supplied. Original source and unassigned fields were not examined; their schema entries are placeholders. Page 5 contains both a reading-condition test and an ART predictor/interaction test; the broad supplied description does not identify the desired model term. Candidate evidence (not assigned values): p. 5 literary versus nonfiction condition: nonfiction (Madj. ⫽ 27.02), F(1, 167) ⫽ 0.08, p ⫽ .775, d ⫽ 0.07.; ART predictor in that model: RMET, F(1, 266) ⫽ 44.22, p ⬍ .001, b ⫽ 0.19; interaction F(1, 266) = 0.24, p = .625. Comparison analytic participant N = 300 is printed on p. 4, but cannot be assigned until the row/model is resolved. Reported_success refers to the authors’ paper-level verdict on immediate reading effects, not to the significant lifetime ART association.
